A_general.open_code_note: The public repository is Postman’s local STDIO server. Official docs say local and remote servers offer the same tool configurations; the repository therefore serves as the direct local equivalent, but does not establish that its exact commit runs at the hosted endpoint.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.postman.com/learn — US Learning Center search configuration.
https://mcp.postman.com/context-graph — US Context Graph configuration; requires Context Graph enabled for the team.
EU counterparts exist at https://mcp.eu.postman.com/minimal, /code, /mcp, /learn, and /context-graph; docs state these support API-key authentication only.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee is stated. A Postman account is required; MCP calls count toward the plan’s monthly Postman API call limits. The endpoint’s unauthenticated response says “API key required,” while US remote documentation describes OAuth access without a key.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free: $0/month; Solo: $9/month billed annually; Team: $19/user/month billed annually; Enterprise: contact sales.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP tool calls count toward plan API-call limits. The reviewed pricing materials did not specify the applicable monthly API-call quotas.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: US remote supports OAuth and Postman API-key authentication. EU remote and local STDIO require an API key. Context Graph configuration requires the feature enabled for the team. Product permissions and plan limits apply.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Postman controls authentication, hosted endpoint configurations, and plan limits; organization/team administrators control access and feature availability through Postman settings and roles.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The supplied endpoint probe returned HTTP 401, WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.postman.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", and JSON-RPC error “Invalid Request: API key required”. Protected-resource metadata identifies https://mcp.postman.com as authorization server. Authorization metadata declares code flow, authorization_code and refresh_token grants, S256 PKCE, DCR at /register, token endpoint auth methods none/client_secret_basic/client_secret_post, and revocation at /revoke. scopes_supported is absent. Token lifetime is not stated. The probe’s key-required message differs from US remote docs describing OAuth without a key.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated endpoint response: HTTP 401 and JSON-RPC error object with code -32600, message “Invalid Request: API key required”, id null.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration; API key. Raw endpoint response: HTTP 401; WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.postman.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"; JSON: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Invalid Request: API key required"},"id":null}. Protected-resource documents name resource https://mcp.postman.com/mcp and authorization_servers ["https://mcp.postman.com"], bearer_methods_supported ["header"]. Authorization metadata: issuer https://mcp.postman.com; authorization_endpoint /authorize; token_endpoint /token; registration_endpoint /register; response_types_supported ["code"]; grant_types_supported ["authorization_code","refresh_token"]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["none","client_secret_basic","client_secret_post"]; revocation_endpoint /revoke; code_challenge_methods_supported ["S256"]. scopes_supported and token lifetime are not supplied.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Full tools include read and write operations. The local-equivalent modules declare MCP annotations including readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint; these are hints, not a server confirmation gate. 2. Hosted docs recommend reviewing changes, but no universal server-enforced confirmation step was found. 3. OAuth metadata has no scopes_supported field; docs say US OAuth and API-key access, with API-key-only EU/local modes. Postman account permissions and team feature settings govern access; token lifetime is not documented. 4. Toolsets are selected by endpoint path; US/EU endpoints differ, and Context Graph requires team enablement. 5. No general MCP-level masking policy was found. Tool schemas/instructions caution against including sensitive variables; product permissions still apply. 6. Calls count toward Postman plan API-call limits. Several tools expose pagination and explicit caps; no universal hosted MCP result cap was found. 7. The local equivalent uses Zod input schemas and converts upstream errors; tool-specific defaults and limits exist. No general hallucinated-argument alias rewriting was found. 8. Hosted telemetry is documented as anonymous and enabled by default. The local code records tool names, argument keys (not values), argument/result sizes, latency, status/error fields, auth method and client-supplied metadata; local telemetry is opt-in. 9. No tool name/description requests feedback, ratings, surveys, or reports. No tool-result upsell mechanism was found in the analyzed public code. 10. Initialization instructions require fetching postman://instructions; additional instruction tools provide API/code guidance. These behavioral rules are agent guidance, not universal server-side enforcement. 11. Local telemetry keeps per-process session data; operations also use Postman resources and asynchronous API tasks. No persistent agent behavior memory was found. 12. Non-flat structure: toolsets are selected by URL/configuration, with US/EU endpoint variants; Context Graph uses submit-and-poll tools and Learning Center search is a separate toolset. 13. No general raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script-execution escape-hatch tool appears in the Full tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Before answering any API-related questions, fetch the MCP resource at URI `postman://instructions` using FetchMcpResource from this MCP server, and follow the usage instructions contained within.
Do NOT rely on your own knowledge of available tools or APIs to answer questions like "is there an API for X?" or "find me an API that does Y."

Always review and confirm operations. When performing operations that make changes or are destructive, such as updating or deleting resources, always validate responses before you accept them from the agent.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The service has distinct URL-selected toolsets (Minimal, Code, Full, Learn, Context Graph) and US/EU endpoint variants. The input /mcp path selects Full. Context Graph also uses a submit/poll workflow.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official overview points to the Postman public-workspace MCP collection as the complete tool list, but its collected page rendered as an empty SPA. The official repository’s Full configuration lists 234 tool names, used here as the direct local-equivalent inventory; official product materials state “100+” with no exact total. No catalogue-only tools were added. Docker MCP Catalog and Ext Ops Panel each report 42 tools, matching the Minimal configuration rather than Full. MCPBundles requires connection to inspect its live list and publishes no count. Claude’s connector page is marked Anthropic verified but gives no tool count. Agent Discoverability reports 231 for a Postman plugin, not this MCP endpoint; Composio’s Postman toolkit is a separate proxy/API surface and was not used.

The MCP connection itself requires an existing account/key or supported OAuth authorization.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The tips page advises: “Always review and confirm operations.” It also says: “Pass resource IDs to reduce API calls.” These are client/agent recommendations; the public code does not impose a general confirmation gate. The initialize instruction tells the agent to fetch and follow the instruction resource.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The product page states: “All communication with the MCP Server happens over HTTPS” and “Postman does not store AI agent prompts or responses.” Remote-server docs say telemetry is anonymous and enabled by default. Public local telemetry code records argument keys rather than argument values, plus call sizes, results sizes, timing, error/auth fields and client-supplied metadata.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The overview describes the remote server as hosted over streamable HTTPS and says remote and local servers provide the same tool configurations. Product materials describe OAuth or API keys as access controls and say MCP calls count against plan API-call limits.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: HTTPS and authentication are consistent with hosted docs and OAuth metadata. The prompt/response non-storage claim is not directly verified by the public local-equivalent code; its telemetry omits argument values but includes metadata fields and result size. The local code’s opt-in telemetry differs from hosted docs’ default-on remote telemetry. Confirmation is recommended in docs but is not a universal server-enforced flow in the local equivalent.

contradictions: The unauthenticated input endpoint returns “API key required,” while Postman’s US remote-server docs describe OAuth without an API key. The same endpoint supplies OAuth protected-resource metadata and advertises an authorization server.

The Postman overview links its public collection as the complete official tool list, but the collected collection pages rendered blank. The repository inventory lists 234 Full tools; product materials only state “100+,” without a conflicting exact count.
Docker MCP Catalog and Ext Ops Panel each show 42 tools for the server; this matches the official Minimal tool configuration and does not represent the input Full endpoint’s tool count.
Agent Discoverability lists 231 tools for a Postman plugin, not the MCP endpoint; it was excluded from actions.
observations_for_research: One hostname exposes materially different tool configurations through URL paths, so the selected endpoint path determines the agent’s available actions.
Hosted US OAuth and EU API-key-only access create region-specific authorization behavior.
Remote telemetry defaults on while local-equivalent telemetry defaults off, according to official setup documentation and public code.
The included instruction resource shapes API discovery behavior by directing agents to search Postman before answering API-availability questions.
